preamble: Place assimilation of the coda tap [ɾ] to a voiced bilabial fricative or approximant [β] before /p/: [β˺p]. In western Cuban Spanish (the provinces from Pinar del Río to Matanzas and Cienfuegos, including Havana, plus the municipalities of Corralillo and Trinidad), coda /ɾ/ and coda /l/ merge and assimilate to the next consonant. Guitart (1978, 2004) describes the first element of rp and lp as non-occlusive [β˺p], against the stop of rb and lb ([b˺b]), and the acoustic study of Ruiz Hernández and Miyares Bermúdez (1984) also lists [βp] beside [bp] (all as summarized by Arias 2019). This is a competing description of the sequence filed under ɾ > b: Arias writes [b˺p] within words (cuerpo cue[b˺p]o) and follows Guitart's [β˺p] across word boundaries, noting that the realization is the same in both positions and the transcriptions differ only because they follow different descriptions. The unassimilated pronunciations remain more common.

examples.note: Across a word boundary; Arias, following Guitart's description, glosses the form as 'mal picado o mar picado', because coda /l/ gives the same result. The sources consulted give only this one example.

sources: Arias Cabal, Á. (2019). Fonética y fonología de las consonantes geminadas en el español de Cuba. Moenia, 25, 465–497. https://revistas.usc.gal/index.php/moenia/article/view/6474
